title: Arriving at the Contracted Event Value Standing at Notice
content:
The contracted event value of a Private Event & Banquet Services booking standing at the moment written notice of cancellation is given is the estimated contracted value standing on the booking entry in the event ledger.

## The three parts of the value

1. **The estimate.** The estimated contracted value standing on the booking entry in the event ledger.
2. **The room rental.** The room rental printed against the package is added to it in full.
3. **The service charge.** The service charge printed against the package is worked on the food and beverage value the contracted value is built on — that being the estimated contracted value standing on the booking entry — and added. No service charge is worked on the room rental, on the audio-visual package or on the dance floor charge.

The contracted value is the estimated value, the room rental and that service charge added together and rounded to two decimal places at the end only, the parts themselves being left unrounded.

## Worked figure on hypothetical records

A booking sits on the Seated Banquet Package. The booking entry in the event ledger records an estimated contracted value of 9000. The package prints a room rental of 950 and a service charge of 22 per cent.

| Part | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Estimated contracted value on the booking entry | 9000 |
| Room rental printed against the package | 950 |
| Service charge, being 22 per cent of 9000 | 1980 |
| Contracted event value, rounded at the end only | 11930.00 |

Had the estimate been 9000.40, the service charge would be 1980.088; the three parts would be carried unrounded into the total of 11930.488, and only that total would be rounded, to 11930.49.

## Points of judgement

The service charge is worked on the food and beverage value the contracted value is built on, never on the room rental added at the second step, so a larger room rental never enlarges the service charge.

Rounding happens once. A part carrying a fraction of a cent is carried into the total as it stands, and the two decimal places are taken on the sum.
